guideTitle: Best Cordless Tool Combo Kits Under $300 (2026)
metaDescription: Five cordless tool combo kits under $300 compared on tools included, battery count, platform depth and whether a 2-tool or 6-tool kit suits a homeowner.
expertTake: Under $300 the best combo kit is the one that gives you the right two or three tools on a battery platform you will keep, and the DEWALT DCK240C2 is the best overall because it pairs a drill and an impact driver with two batteries, a charger and a bag. The RYOBI P1819 is the best value for breadth with six tools on a platform of over 125, the BLACK+DECKER four-tool kit is the easy starter and the CRAFTSMAN V20 pair is the lowest-cost name-brand duo. The TEENO 9-in-1 is a novelty. Skip big kits if you will only ever drill and drive.
introParagraphs: A combo kit bundles several cordless tools and shares one battery platform among them, which is why it is the cheapest way to build a toolbox. The trade-off is that you also buy the tools you did not choose, and the batteries in a kit are usually small to keep the price down.

This guide explains how to judge a kit by the tools in it and the platform behind it, which compromises are fine for a homeowner and which will leave you buying a second kit within a year. The quick picks are above, and the reviews below match each kit to a type of household.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX DCK240C2 Drill and Impact Driver Combo Kit, 2 Batteries
products.description:
The DCK240C2 is the best buy because it gives you the two tools most households use every week, on a platform that will serve you for decades. A drill and an impact driver are a natural pair: the drill makes holes and drives small screws with a clutch, while the impact driver sinks long screws without stalling. The drill is rated at up to 300 unit watts out, a measure of delivered power that is more honest than a peak torque figure.

Two batteries mean one can charge while the other works, which matters more than any tool spec when you are doing an afternoon project. The tools are compact and designed to fit in tight spaces, and a contractor bag carries everything. Against the CRAFTSMAN pair, which is also a drill and impact driver, the DEWALT sits on a platform that spans hundreds of tools and gets better resale.

The cost of buying into DEWALT is that further tools cost more than on RYOBI or CRAFTSMAN. Even so, bare tools on 20V MAX go on sale regularly. Keep the batteries cool and avoid leaving them in a hot truck, which ages lithium cells. Keep the second battery on the charger so it is ready when the first drains.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a durable drill and impact driver pair on a platform they can grow.
pros: Drill and impact driver cover most household work
Two batteries and a charger in the kit
Drill rated up to 300 UWO
Platform spans hundreds of tools
cons: Only two tools in the kit
Additional tools cost more than on RYOBI

products.name: RYOBI P1819 18V ONE+ 6-Tool Combo Kit, 2 Batteries and Bag

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: Drill/driver, impact driver, reciprocating saw, circular saw and more

products.description:
The RYOBI P1819 is the best value for breadth. It bundles six tools: a drill/driver, an impact driver, a reciprocating saw, a circular saw and two others, with two batteries, a charger, a bag and accessories. For a first-time homeowner, that covers drilling, driving, demolition and cutting in one purchase.

The ONE+ platform is the other half of the value. Over 125 tools run on the same 18V battery, from string trimmers to inflators to a nailer, so the batteries you buy here will power the yard, the garage and the car. Compared with the DEWALT kit, the RYOBI gives you three times as many tools for a comparable outlay, though each tool is a lighter-duty design.

The batteries in a six-tool kit are modest, so a long session of sawing will drain them. Treat the saws as occasional-use tools and keep the batteries charged. If you only ever need a drill and an impact driver, the DEWALT or CRAFTSMAN pair is the better buy, but if you want a full starter shop, this is it. Learn the clutch settings on the drill, since they protect screws and workpieces.
products.bestFor: First-time homeowners who want a full starter toolbox on a broad, affordable platform.
pros: Six tools cover drilling, driving, sawing and demolition
Platform of over 125 tools on one battery
Two batteries, a charger and a bag included
Lowest cost per tool of any kit here
cons: Small batteries drain in long sessions
Some included tools you may never use

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX BD4KITCDCRL 4-Tool Combo Kit, 2 Batteries

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: Drill/driver, circular saw, work light and more

products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER four-tool kit is the starter for people who want the basics at a low price. Its drill has a 3/8 inch chuck, a top speed of 650 rpm and an 11-position clutch, specifications aimed at consumer projects like furniture assembly and shelf hanging. A 650 rpm top speed is slow for drilling and fine for driving screws, so treat it as a driver first.

The circular saw has a 5-1/2 inch blade, small enough to be light and large enough to cut 2x lumber, and the work light claims up to 11 hours of runtime. Two batteries and a charger complete the package. Compared with the RYOBI, you get fewer tools, and compared with the DEWALT, you get a lighter-duty drill but a saw and a light.

The platform is the POWERCONNECT 20V MAX line, which shares batteries with a range of home tools like trimmers and vacuums. It is an easy first step and an easy platform to extend, though it will not stand up to daily use. For a household that needs to hang pictures, build a bookshelf and cut a few boards, it is enough. Replace dull blades and bits promptly, because they strain tools and shorten battery life.
products.bestFor: New homeowners who want a simple, low-cost set for assembly and light projects.
pros: Drill, saw and work light in one kit
11-position clutch protects screws
5-1/2 inch saw cuts 2x lumber
Batteries fit other home tools

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Drill Driver and Impact Driver Combo, 2 x 2Ah Batteries

specList.label: Claimed runtime
specList.value: Up to 90 holes per charge (maker figure)

specList.label: Impact driver
specList.value: Rated for deck screws to lag bolts

products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN pair is the lowest-cost name-brand drill and impact driver duo. The drill matches the DEWALT's 300 UWO rating and claims about 90 holes per charge, a maker figure that assumes small holes in softwood. The impact driver is marketed for fastening from deck screws to lag bolts, a bold claim for a consumer tool.

It includes two 2 Ah batteries and a charger, the same battery count as the DEWALT. A second listing sells the same kit with a single battery, so check which one you are buying. Against the DEWALT, the CRAFTSMAN gives up some brand depth and resale value, but it is cheaper and sits on a growing V20 platform with bare tools for trimming, blowing and sawing.

Both tools are brushed designs, so they suit occasional use. If you drive a lot of screws, the DEWALT's reputation may be worth the extra, and if you want a full shop, the RYOBI is the better buy. For a simple pair at the lowest name-brand price, this is it. Keep the batteries cool and charged. Store the kit in its bag in a dry place, away from heat.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a drill and impact driver pair from an established brand.
pros: Lowest-cost name-brand drill and impact driver pair
Drill rated up to 300 UWO
Two 2 Ah batteries and a charger
V20 platform has bare tools to add
cons: A single-battery listing of the same kit exists

products.name: TEENO 9-in-1 Brushless 20V Interchangeable Cordless Tool Set, 2 x 4.0Ah

specList.label: Format
specList.value: One brushless power head with 9 attachments

specList.label: Attachments
specList.value: Drill, impact, grinder, sander and more

specList.label: Motor
specList.value: Brushless, up to 50% more runtime (maker claim)

products.description:
The TEENO 9-in-1 is the most unusual kit here: one brushless motor head and nine interchangeable attachments, including a drill, an impact driver, a grinder and a sander. The idea is to buy one motor and swap heads, which saves the cost of nine separate motors. Two 4.0 Ah batteries are larger than any other pack in this guide.

A modular system trades convenience for capability. Every head runs on the same motor, so each is limited to what that motor can deliver, and switching heads takes time. A dedicated impact driver or grinder will outperform its attachment equivalent. The maker claims up to 50 percent more runtime for the brushless motor, a claim that depends on the comparison.

It makes sense for hobbyists with limited storage who do many different light jobs, and less sense for anyone who drills and drives daily. Against the RYOBI, which gives six separate tools, the TEENO gives nine heads on one motor. If one head breaks you lose that function, and if the motor fails you lose all nine, so check the warranty. Treat it as an experiment, not a platform.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists with limited storage who want many functions from one motor.
pros: Nine attachments on one brushless motor
Two 4.0 Ah batteries are the largest here
Compact storage compared with separate tools
Brushless motor improves efficiency
cons: Switching heads is slower than switching tools
One motor failure disables every attachment

buyingCriteria.explanation: A drill and an impact driver cover most household work, and both the DEWALT and CRAFTSMAN kits give you exactly that. The RYOBI adds saws and the BLACK+DECKER adds a saw and light. Count the tools you will use in a year, because extra tools in a kit are only worth the cost if they get used. If you already own one battery brand, buying a kit on another platform means two chargers and two sets of batteries to manage.

A kit's batteries decide how much you can do in a session. The DEWALT, RYOBI, CRAFTSMAN and BLACK+DECKER each ship with two batteries, mostly in the 1.5 to 2 Ah range, while the TEENO ships two 4.0 Ah packs. Two batteries beat one big one because you can swap and keep working. A kit with an impact driver and a drill lets you set the drill to a low clutch for screws and keep the impact driver for lag screws.

The ONE+ platform has over 125 tools, DEWALT 20V MAX has hundreds, CRAFTSMAN V20 and BLACK+DECKER POWERCONNECT have large home-oriented lineups, and the TEENO has little. A kit is the entry fee to a platform, so choose the one that has the next tools you will want. Many first-time buyers overbuy the number of tools, then find the saws are used once a year.

Most budget kits, including the DEWALT, RYOBI, CRAFTSMAN and BLACK+DECKER, use brushed tools, which cost less and are fine for occasional use. Brushless tools last longer and run longer per charge. The TEENO is the only brushless kit here. Spare batteries are the real long-term cost, so check what a single replacement pack costs on each platform.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Torque and speed in the drill
buyingCriteria.explanation: The DEWALT and CRAFTSMAN drills are rated up to 300 UWO, while the BLACK+DECKER drill has a 3/8 inch chuck and a 650 rpm top speed. A 1/2 inch chuck and a two-speed gearbox are worth having. For heavy drilling, favor the higher UWO rating. Charge time matters in practice, since a 60-minute charger is much more useful than a 3-hour one.

A good kit includes a bag and a charger that fits the batteries. The DEWALT and RYOBI include bags. Look for a charger rated to refill a 2 Ah battery in about an hour, since a slow charger makes two batteries feel like one. A bag that keeps everything together saves more time than another tool in the kit.

specDecoder.meaning: A measure of power delivered at the chuck, combining speed and torque. Unit watts out is a manufacturer metric used mostly by DEWALT and CRAFTSMAN, so it is not available for every kit.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT and CRAFTSMAN both quote up to 300 UWO.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity. A 4.0 Ah pack stores twice the energy of a 2.0 Ah pack. A 20V MAX pack is not stronger than an 18V pack, only named differently.
specDecoder.watchFor: A kit with two small batteries can still run out in a long saw session.

specDecoder.meaning: 20V MAX is peak voltage, and the nominal voltage is 18V. Cordless saws drain batteries faster than drills, so judge battery size by the heaviest tool.
specDecoder.watchFor: RYOBI's 18V and DEWALT's 20V MAX are the same class.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum bit shank the drill accepts. 3/8 inch is light-duty and 1/2 inch is standard. A 2 Ah pack is light but small, so heavy use needs spares.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BLACK+DECKER drill has a 3/8 inch chuck.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor without brushes that runs cooler and lasts longer. Interchangeable heads share a motor, so their limits are the motor's limits.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the TEENO lists brushless here.

maintenance.task: Store batteries cool and part charged
maintenance.why: Heat and full charge age lithium cells. Remove batteries before changing bits.
Dust causes slipping. Wipe dust from the tools.
A dull blade strains tools and batteries. Check chargers for damage.
Blocked vents overheat motors. Inspect the bag zipper.
Long storage lets cells drift. Store batteries dry.

faq.q: Is a combo kit cheaper than buying tools separately?
faq.a: Usually yes. A kit bundles batteries and a charger at a discount. Read the contents list carefully, since two kits with similar names can include different tools.
Choose the one with the next tools you will want, such as garden or garage tools. Check that a replacement battery is sold separately for the platform you choose.

faq.q: How many batteries do I need?
faq.a: Two. One charges while the other works. Register the kit for the warranty and keep the receipt.
For occasional use, yes. Brushless lasts longer and runs longer.
No. Batteries do not cross platforms without adapters.
It saves storage but each head is limited. It is best for light hobby use.
